sourceNote: Core sites from Wikipedia Geosearch API. Elephanta Caves, Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, Banganga Tank, Marine Drive, Dharavi, Sanjay Gandhi NP, Juhu Beach added as curated. All records needs_review.

places.name: Gateway of India
places.description: Iconic 26m basalt arch overlooking Mumbai Harbour, built in 1924 to commemorate King George V's visit. The focal point of South Mumbai's waterfront; ferry departures to Elephanta Caves leave from here. Crowds peak late afternoon. Free to access; always busy with vendors and tourists.

places.name: Elephanta Caves
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site — rock-cut cave temples on Elephanta Island, 10km from the Gateway of India. The main Shiva cave features the magnificent trimurti (three-faced Shiva) sculpture from the 5th–8th century. Accessible by 1-hour ferry from Gateway of India (45 min each way). Budget a full half-day. The island and caves closed on Mondays.

places.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Victorian Gothic railway station completed in 1888, designed by F. W. Stevens. Also known as Victoria Terminus (VT); a working railway station with ornate domes, turrets, pointed arches and gargoyles. Best viewed from outside; interior accessible as an active station. Photography from the exterior freely available.

places.name: Marine Drive (Queen's Necklace)
places.description: 3.6km arc-shaped promenade and road along the Arabian Sea from Nariman Point to Chowpatty Beach. The city lights reflected in the sea at night create the famous Queen's Necklace effect. Popular morning and evening jogging circuit; best at sunset or after dark. Free, open all hours.

places.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
places.description: Formerly the Prince of Wales Museum; Mumbai's premier museum with collections of Indian art, natural history and decorative arts. Housed in an Indo-Saracenic building in Kala Ghoda. Strong Harappan, Tibetan Buddhist art and miniature painting collections. Budget 2 hours.

places.name: Kala Ghoda Arts District
places.description: South Mumbai's arts precinct centred on K Dubash Marg, housing galleries, museums, bookshops, cafés and street art. Hosts the annual Kala Ghoda Arts Festival each February. Good area for street food and walking between the museum, Jehangir Gallery and historic Fort architecture.

places.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
places.description: 104 sq km national park within Greater Mumbai — one of the few national parks inside a city. Leopards, deer, birds and the 2nd–3rd century BC Kanheri Caves are accessible within the park. Good early-morning wildlife spotting. The Kanheri Caves alone require a half-day; the full park needs planning.

places.name: Juhu Beach
places.description: Mumbai's most popular public beach, 6km long in the Juhu suburb. Not suitable for swimming but a lively evening destination with street food stalls selling bhel puri, pani puri and corn on the cob. Good for people-watching and sunsets. Near several Bollywood stars' homes.

places.name: Banganga Tank
places.description: Ancient sacred tank on Malabar Hill believed to have been created by Rama, featuring small temples and ghats around the water. One of Mumbai's oldest Hindu sites (12th century) and a surprising peaceful oasis in the dense urban fabric. Atmospheric and photogenic in early morning.

places.name: Dharavi
places.description: One of Asia's largest urban settlements, Dharavi is a hub of small-scale industries including leather, pottery, textiles and food processing. Guided slum tours operate with community benefit; controversial but give insights into informal urban economies. Book through responsible tour operators. Not a spectator attraction; engage through a guided tour.

places.name: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel
places.description: 1903 heritage hotel beside the Gateway of India, considered one of the world's great historic hotels. External architecture is a landmark of South Mumbai. Non-guests can visit the lobby and restaurants. The Sea Lounge afternoon tea is a popular option.

places.name: Haji Ali Dargah
places.description: 15th-century Sufi mosque and dargah on a tiny tidal islet connected to Worli by a narrow 500m causeway, accessible only at low tide. Housing the tomb of Muslim merchant Haji Ali Bukhari, it is one of Mumbai's most visited pilgrimage sites by both Muslims and Hindus. The causeway can flood during high tide; check tide times.
places.openingDays: Daily 05:30–22:00 (causeway accessible 6 hours around low tide)

places.name: Siddhivinayak Temple
places.description: One of Mumbai's most visited and financially wealthy temples, dedicated to Lord Ganesha. Built in 1801; enormously popular before exams, new ventures and Tuesdays (Ganesha's day). Very long queues on peak days; arrive before 07:00 for shorter wait. Celebrity visitors are common.

places.name: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site comprising two distinct 19th–20th century architectural clusters facing each other across the Oval Maidan in South Mumbai. Victorian Gothic buildings (University of Mumbai, High Court, Rajabai Clock Tower) face art deco residential buildings and cinemas. Best experienced on a walking tour.

places.name: Mumbai Vada Pav and Bhel Puri Walk
places.description: Mumbai's street food trinity: vada pav (spicy potato fritter in pav), bhel puri (puffed rice salad), and pav bhaji (spiced vegetable mash with butter-toasted rolls). Juhu Beach for bhel, Anand Stall at Vile Parle for vada pav, and Sardar for pav bhaji near Tardeo.

places.name: Britannia & Co — Parsi Dhansak
places.description: One of Mumbai's most iconic Parsi restaurants (est. 1923), in the Fort district. Famous for dhansak (lamb/chicken with lentils and rice), mutton berry pulao, and caramel custard. Run by the Kohinoor family, it's a living piece of Irani café culture and Bombay heritage.
